voyage.name: Easter
voyage.content: Egg fights!

voyage.name: Count of May
voyage.content: Medieval festival. Takes place annually in mid-May.

voyage.name: Latviabeerfest
voyage.content: Takes place annually at the end of May. The largest international beer festival in the Baltics.

voyage.name: Jāņi
voyage.content: On June 24, Latvians celebrate the summer solstice with the midsummer festival called Jāņi. Before the celebration, flea markets are held in many places.

voyage.name: Latvian Song and Dance Festival
voyage.alt: Latvian Vispārējie latviešu Dziesmu un Deju svētki
voyage.hours: Takes place once every 5 years, at the beginning of July
voyage.address: Mežaparka Lielā estrāde or Vērmanes garden, Riga
voyage.content: One of the key cultural events in Latvia, which started in 1873 as a singing festival. This festival has become an important facet of Latvian culture and has been held 25 times since then. There are smaller Song and Dance Festivals between 5-year time spans. About 30,000 people from every corner of the country participate, with choirs and dance groups at the heart of the celebrations. Brass bands, folk ensembles, pla

voyage.name: Rīga City Day
voyage.hours: Takes place the whole of August
voyage.content: Traditional weekend of celebrating a city. Many cultural events take place all around the city.

voyage.name: White Night
voyage.hours: Annually, in the beginning of September

voyage.name: Riga Rhythms Festival
voyage.price: Some events cost €10-45, some are free
voyage.hours: Takes place annually, at the end of June/start of July; 18:00–00:00

voyage.name: Lattelecom Marathon
voyage.hours: Held in the middle of May
voyage.content: The biggest sport marathon held since 2007 in Latvia.

voyage.name: Playground
voyage.content: Youth sport festival that encourages and enables every visitor to try to explore inspiring sports and culture on water, land and air (e.g. longboarding, SUP, wakeboarding, hydro-cycles, mountain bikes, slack line).

voyage.name: Čili Pica
voyage.content: Cheap but good pizza.

voyage.name: Lido
voyage.content: A network of 8 restaurants offering decent hearty Latvian food, including desserts, at good prices. The restaurants are either cafeteria-style or feature English menus.

voyage.name: Triangula Bastion
voyage.content: A modern building with an excavated fragment of the historical fortification wall system along the river. The building has the best view terraces in Riga.

voyage.name: Statue of Roland
voyage.content: Statue of St. Roland, the patron of Riga. The original statue erected in 1897 was destroyed in World War II; now a replica stands there.

voyage.name: House of the Blackheads
voyage.content: The House of Blackheads is where the merchants-to-be had their guild. Part of this building is the tourist information office, the rest is a fascinating museum. The upper levels house grand ballrooms while the basement has a wine cellar and several exhibits relating to trading in Riga.

voyage.name: Town Hall
voyage.content: Pretty to look at, but not open for visitors.

voyage.name: Bremen Town Musicians
voyage.content: Amazing sculpture based on a fairy tale by the Brothers Grimm.

voyage.name: 1905 Bloody Sunday Monument
voyage.content: This monument remembrance of the events of Bloody Sunday 13 January 1905.

voyage.name: House of Dannenstern
voyage.content: The house was built by and is named after Ernst Metue von Dannenstern.

voyage.name: Riga monument to Christmas tree
voyage.content: First Christmas tree in Riga was in 1510!

voyage.name: The Large Guild
voyage.content: Housed the guild of the tradesmen, who would join after being a member of the Blackheads (see House of Blackheads). Home to the Latvian Philharmonic – you can't just walk inside. It's the exterior that's worth seeing though.

voyage.name: The Small Guild
voyage.content: Another pretty building just behind the Big Guild, this one housed the craftsmen's guild. Like the Big Guild, you can't go inside except for a performance.

voyage.name: The House of the Black Cat
voyage.content: This building (also housing a pub of no particular note) is most famous for the two statues of black cats on the roofs. The legend has it that a disgruntled tradesman who was not accepted into the Big Guild, built this house and put the cats on it with their tails pointing towards the Big Guild, thus expressing his scorn.

voyage.name: Wagner Concert Hall
voyage.content: Wagner once lived in Riga, on the street now named after him. This hall where he performed occasionally holds concerts.

voyage.name: Museum of the Occupation of Latvia
voyage.content: This noticeable and austere black building is clearly out-of-place. In the Soviet days, this housed a museum to the Red Riflemen, a group of Latvians who volunteered for the service to Russia during the Russian revolution of 1917. Now it houses a museum of Latvia's time under the Nazi and Soviet occupations. Very long, but very moving – essential for anyone interested in the history of the USSR or Nazi Germany. Outsi

voyage.name: Museum of Decorative Arts and Design
voyage.content: The Museum of Decorative and Design Art is located in the former St. George’s Church building (1204), which is the oldest stone building in Riga. It features seven collections of decorative and design art work.

voyage.name: Riga Film Museum
voyage.address: Peitavas iela 10 (Entrance from Mazā Peitavas Street)
voyage.content: This museum holds various exhibitions that display different aspects of cinema art, actors and film history.

voyage.name: Porcelain Museum
voyage.content: Covers the history of porcelain in Riga through the 19th and 20th centuries.

voyage.name: Latvian Sports Museum
voyage.price: Adults €0.71; school children, students, seniors €0.43; children aged 6 and under, people with disabilities free
voyage.content: Historic sports equipment and sportswear, photographs from a variety of sporting events.

voyage.name: Latvian artists union museum
voyage.content: The collection covers the period from 1945 to 1991 in Latvia.

voyage.name: Sun Museum
voyage.content: One of Riga's weirdest museums, it covers the history of sun mythology and its role in Latvian culture.

voyage.name: Latvian National Museum of Art
voyage.content: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art.

voyage.name: National History Museum of Latvia
voyage.content: The History Museum is interesting, however there is little English (every room has its exhibits summarized on a single plaque). However, the museum does give a very good idea of Latvian history, and will give you a good understanding of the area.

voyage.name: Latvian Photographic Museum
voyage.content: Contains photos of Latvia since 1839, with focuses on the World Wars and 1905 Revolution.

voyage.name: Riga Photonics Center
voyage.content: Riga Photonics Center is part of University of Latvia. Occasional events.

voyage.name: Riga Fashion museum
voyage.price: Adults €7; pupils, students and seniors €5; children under 5 years free
voyage.content: Only fashion museum in the Baltics, created in one of the most popular tourist attractions in Old Riga opposite to the House of the Blackheads.

voyage.name: Museum of Ancient Baltic Jewellery
voyage.content: The Museum of Ancient Baltic Jewellery was established by two well-known Latvian jewellers.

voyage.name: LUMAS Riga
voyage.content: LUMAS Art Gallery offer latest movements in the young art scene.

voyage.name: Art Gallery Bastejs
voyage.content: Contemporary art from Baltic states. Solo and group exhibitions.

voyage.name: Art Gallery Putti
voyage.content: Riga art gallery since 2000.

voyage.name: St. Peter's Church
voyage.content: St. Peter's Church, dating to 1209, is Riga's oldest church. Besides its ensemble of architecture, the church has an elevator to the tower from where you can see all of Riga (service not available on Mondays).

voyage.name: St. John's Church
voyage.content: A smaller, less spectacular church near Saint Peter's. There is a nice altar inside, and unlike most Riga churches, this one is free. The altar is from the Renaissance period and depicts the death, resurrection and ascension of Jesus. The ceiling is from the Gothic period, and has 5 separate vaulted compartments. There is also a huge pipe organ, and many stained glass windows. This church dates back to the mid 1200s.

voyage.name: St. Saviour's Anglican Church
voyage.content: Riga's only Anglican church has English language services every Sunday at 11:00, and free concerts every Wednesday.

voyage.name: St. Jacob's Catholic Church
voyage.content: Dating to 1226, this is one of the few Catholic churches left in Riga. At one point, it housed one of Riga's first schools.

voyage.name: Riga Castle
voyage.content: One of the medieval castles in Latvia, on the bank of the river, which is now the seat of the Latvian president. The museum in the castle can be visited by the public.

voyage.name: Great Kristaps
voyage.content: Great Kristaps is popular with film industry people.

voyage.name: Peter I house
voyage.content: House what was gifted to Peter I and house he visited during his travels.

voyage.name: The Three Brothers
voyage.content: The oldest dwelling houses in Riga. One of them has a small architecture museum inside, along with changing exhibits about Latvia.

voyage.name: Latvian Parliament
voyage.content: A rather plain building housing the Saeima, Latvia's parliament. It has had a number of uses, including as a Soviet-era museum. Not open to visitors.

voyage.name: Swedish Gate
voyage.content: The last remaining gate from the old city walls.

voyage.name: Woman with amphora
voyage.content: Statue of woman with amphora on a building.

voyage.name: Art Museum Riga Bourse
voyage.content: The Art Museum Riga Bourse stores the largest collection of foreign art in the Baltic states.

voyage.name: Museum of the Barricades of 1991
voyage.content: Covers the dramatic events that occurred in the tumultuous final year of the USSR, when Soviet authorities sent troops into Riga to overthrow the elected Latvian government.

voyage.name: Museum of the History of Riga and Navigation
voyage.content: Actually two museums plus a number of special exhibits, though you pay one price. English, German and Russian descriptions of each permanent collections are provided in a booklet inside each exhibit hall. Both of the main museums are quite interesting, and they provide a good idea of what Riga was like in the past.

voyage.name: Arsenal Museum of Art
voyage.content: Arsenal Museum of Art is one of the largest exhibition halls in Riga. It is located in an important architectural monument – a customs warehouse or arsenal built at the beginning of the 19th century in the late Russian Classicism style. It was adapted for museum use in the second half of the 1980s.

voyage.name: Literature and music museum
voyage.content: For about 50 years it was a large union of memorial houses devoted to a range of writers. The latest reorganisation in 2009 has resulted in more simple and recognizable establishment – Literature and Music Museum.

voyage.name: Riga Cathedral
voyage.content: Dating to 1207, the cathedral is one of Riga's symbols. The 6768-pipe organ inside is particularly spectacular. Besides the organ, however, the interior is rather Spartan, and may not be worth the entrance fee (even the organ is being restored, though).

voyage.name: St. Mary Magdalene's Catholic Church
voyage.content: St. Mary Magdalene's Church was made of stone in late 13th century. You can find perpetual worship nearby.

voyage.name: Our Lady of Sorrows Church
voyage.content: First stone church built in Riga after the Reformation had reached Livonia.

voyage.name: Gallery Makslas Banka
voyage.content: Individual and group fine art gallery.

voyage.name: St. Jacob's Barracks
voyage.content: The primary attraction here is the last remaining stretch of city wall directly opposite the barracks.

voyage.name: Museum of War
voyage.content: 22 collections of Latvian and Soviet military equipment starting from World War I until today.

voyage.name: Latvian Museum of Pharmacy
voyage.content: In a renovated 18th-century house. The museum showcases pharmaceutical equipment, traditional medicine and herbs and what pharmacies looked like a century ago.

voyage.name: Mentzendorff House
voyage.content: Former residence of a wealthy merchant built in 1720, now a museum dedicated to life in Riga in the 17th & 18th centuries.

voyage.name: Laima Clock
voyage.content: Laima is a Latvian chocolate manufacturer and means good luck in Latvian. The Clock is a traditional meeting place for people in Riga.

voyage.name: Art gallery "Jēkabs"
voyage.content: Jēkabs art gallery offers exhibitions and fine art auctions.

voyage.name: Latvian National Opera
voyage.content: A pretty building in its own right, this is also a nice place to see an opera or ballet.

voyage.name: Latvian National Symphonic Orchestra
voyage.content: It is a team of highly professional musicians with strong traditions, generous sound and devoted performance.

voyage.name: Theater-Club "Hamlets"
voyage.content: Riga Theater-Club in heart of old city.

voyage.name: Mikhail Chekhov Riga Russian Theater
voyage.hours: the booking-office is open daily from 12:00 till 19:00
voyage.content: Oldest Russian theatre in the world outside Russia.

voyage.name: Bastion Hill
voyage.address: Between Raina Bulvaris and Basteja Bulvaris
voyage.content: A small, pleasant park surrounding Brivibas Bulvaris. Sites in the Bastejkalns include a Chinese and a Japanese building, and the Bridge of Love over the Pilsetas Canal. The Bridge of Love has several locks on the railings put up by recently married couples. There is also a memorial to the two people killed here in the tumultuous events of 1991.

voyage.name: Galerija Centrs
voyage.content: A Latvian shopping mall experience.

voyage.name: Convent Yard
voyage.content: A former convent courtyard that now contains several touristy shops.

voyage.name: LIDO Alus Seta
voyage.content: Literally Beer Yard. Serves huge portions of excellent meat and two veg from a grill at the front of the tavern, as well as an excellent choice of beer. Probably the best value place in town, with two courses easily costing less than €7.

voyage.name: Wok to Walk
voyage.content: The Latvian location of the international chain of stir-fry restaurants. Choose your ingredients and watch them being cooked in a giant wok.

voyage.name: Alus Arsenals
voyage.content: A nice, cozy restaurant in the Riga old town serving various meat and fish oriented dishes with quality local beer. Located right next to the Riga castle so it's easy to find. The actual interior of the restaurant is in a cellar, but in summertime, the restaurant features a spacious outdoor terrace.

voyage.name: Fat Pumpkin
voyage.content: Delicious vegan food.

voyage.name: Gardenia at Hotel Garden Palace
voyage.content: Mediterranean and European cuisine. Cosy and elegantly casual restaurant.

voyage.name: Vecmeita ar kaķi
voyage.content: This restaurant and bar is a more upmarket option than Lido, serving very good Latvian food.

voyage.name: Rozengrāls
voyage.content: An authentic medieval restaurant in a real medieval basement in the Old Town. Serves tasty medieval foods and beverages.

voyage.name: Steiku Haoss
voyage.content: As is evident from the name, the restaurant focuses on steaks. There are steaks of every kind of beef cut imaginable, and the price depends on the cut. The quality of the steaks is pretty much close to the best in Riga. The meat is tender, juicy and extremely tasty. Note however that by ordering a steak, you only get the actual meat. Side dishes, such as potatoes, cost extra, as do sauces. Combining all these, you ca

voyage.name: Mārtiņa Beķereja
voyage.content: Traditional Latvian café, popular amongst locals. Always fresh pastry. Cash only sales. There are five Mārtiņa Beķereja cafés in Riga. Vaļņu iela 28 is located in Old Town Riga.

voyage.name: Backpackers Pub
voyage.content: Riga’s first Aussie pub promises to provide plenty of authentic down under atmosphere, but thankfully without any stuffed koalas, Fosters beer posters or, God forbid, any portraits of Paul Hogan. Spread out across three floors, the pub offers 12 local beers on draught for affordable prices served from a bar that’s actually an old VW combi van. Live bands play frequently in the basement and if the cheap happy hour pri

voyage.name: Cuba Cafe
voyage.content: Cozy bar with DJs in the evenings. Salsa dancing on Tuesdays starting at 21:00. 2-for-1 drinks during happy hour (17:00-19:00).

voyage.name: FolkKlubs Ala Pagrabs
voyage.content: Huge beer selection with 28 beers on tap, folk dancing, live music performances, and great authentic food.

voyage.name: Kiwi Bar
voyage.content: Sports bar with karaoke nights.

voyage.name: Paddy Whelans Irish Pub & Sports Bar
voyage.content: A popular Irish bar.

voyage.name: Funny Fox Bar
voyage.content: A karaoke and sports bar. Great place to duck in and have a few jars. A very wide selection of songs and drinks, with a great atmosphere and stuff on the TVs. The karaoke is really fun and it's an intimate setting.

voyage.name: Black Magic
voyage.content: A very cool place with a decor that will remind you of Harry Potter or Lord of the Rings. Very atmospheric. Perhaps the best place to try different types of black balsam, with flights and tastings here, lots of flavors to choose from. All of it is reasonably priced for the experience, and there are also chocolates and other delicacies for sale.

voyage.name: Kalku Varti
voyage.content: Ground-level restaurant with nightclub in the basement.

voyage.name: Shot Café
voyage.content: Popular with young Latvians.

voyage.name: Pūce
voyage.price: Entrance: free + face control. Beer: €2-3, Long drinks: €4-6, Cocktails: €6-9
voyage.content: A trendy place popular with a younger crowd. The main floor has a dance floor with rock and pop music while the basement has a room with techno and/or alternative sounds. It is a very busy place on Th F Sa and is closed on Su M.

voyage.name: Doma Hostel
voyage.content: Clean, safe, cheap, and in a great location. Friendly and helpful staff. Free coffee and tea.

voyage.name: Blue Bird Capsule Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly, English-speaking staff. Capsule hotel style.

voyage.name: Naughty Squirrel Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: Comfortable beds with curtains for privacy and darkness. Offers adrenalin tours, pub crawls, hockey game excursions, and other communal activities. 24-hour reception. Reception sells beer. Free shot of Riga Balsams upon check-in. Friendly staff.

voyage.name: Red Nose Hostel
voyage.content: Red Nose hostel is on a quiet and narrow cobbled backstreet of Old Town, just behind St.Jana church.

voyage.name: Riga Old Town Hostel
voyage.content: En suite rooms, very popular bar, sauna, and 24-hour reception.

voyage.name: Kolonna Hotel Riga
voyage.content: 41 rooms.

voyage.name: Metropole Hotel
voyage.content: Not quite as central as some other hotels, but still quite near Old Town. All rooms have satellite TV and minibar.

voyage.name: Old City Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: The Old City Boutique Hotel is a 4-star hotel and has a central location in Riga’s Old Town.

voyage.name: Old Riga Hotel Vecriga
voyage.content: Old Riga Hotel Vecriga is located in the historical and cultural centre of Riga, on an ancient Gleznotaju street (Painters’ and Goldsmiths’ Street).

voyage.name: Rixwell Old Riga Palace Hotel
voyage.content: In a quiet street in Riga’s Old Town, within walking distance from all the main attractions.

voyage.name: Rixwell Centra Hotel
voyage.content: In a historic building.

voyage.name: Hotel Garden Palace
voyage.content: Elegant boutique hotel with 65 guest rooms.

voyage.name: Neiburgs Hotel
voyage.content: 55 suites. Large, clean, modern rooms.

voyage.name: Pullman Riga Old Town
voyage.content: Opened in 2016 and housed in a complex of buildings including what is said to have been Baron Muenchhausen's stables, the Pullman carries the equine theme in its decor, while adapting Pullman's modern feel and standards to the historic construction. The top-floor pool with views over the area is certainly a highlight.

voyage.name: Wellton Riverside SPA Hotel
voyage.price: EUR 100 and up depending on season
voyage.content: 4-star hotel with the most expensive rooms directly overviewing the Daugava River. On the 8th floor there is access to a splendid rooftop deck with a panoramic view of all sides of the building, including the river.

voyage.name: Freedom Monument
voyage.content: One of Latvia's national symbols. It was erected during the first independence and surprisingly never taken down by the Soviets (although laying flowers at its feet was forbidden). The statue of a woman holding three stars at the top of the monument represents Freedom embracing Latvia's regions.

voyage.name: Art Nouveau Buildings
voyage.content: Alberta and Elizabetes streets (iela) are the best place to see the creations of Art Nouveau architect Eisenstein, famous of his splendid style. Other Art Nouveau buildings can be seen in the area around the Freedom Monument, including the embassies on Raina Bulvaris and on Strelnieku iela.

voyage.name: Kobe Clock
voyage.content: Donated by Riga's sister city Kobe in celebration of anniversary of restoration of independence.

voyage.name: Museum 'Jews in Latvia' and Jewish Community
voyage.content: Small museum dedicated to Jewish life in Latvia since the 16th century. Includes information on destruction of the synagogues by the Nazis, and the Latvians that saved Jews during the Holocaust. Exhibits are in English and Latvian.

voyage.name: National Museum of Art
voyage.content: Latvian National Museum of Art is the most significant depository in the nation for works of art. Houses many works by Latvian artists.

voyage.name: Former KGB Building
voyage.price: exhibition free, €5 for a guided tour of the KGB cellar
voyage.content: The former KGB building is actually an attractive, ornate historic building at the corner of Brivibas and Stabu. It stood empty for years, but for the 2014 celebration of Riga becoming the European Capital of Culture it was revived with a number of artistic initiatives taking place there. It is now a branch of the Museum of the Occupation of Latvia, holding a general exhibition about the KGB activities, and guided to

voyage.name: Riga Orthodox Cathedral
voyage.content: The Orthodox Cathedral was erected during Russian rule for Russian residents. In contrast to its relatively plain exterior, it is spectacular on the inside, but be aware that shorts are not allowed.

voyage.name: St. Gertrude Old Church
voyage.content: The brick neogothic church of St. Getrude, despite "old" in its name, is an entirely late 19th-century creation that replaced a series of stone and wooden churches that stood there (and were repeatedly destroyed due to being outside of the city walls) since the 15th century. The unusual veracity with which the 19th-century architects interpreted the principles of Gothic architecture may make the church pass for an au

voyage.name: Choral Great Synagogue
voyage.content: Mostly in ruins since the Germans burned it down on July 4, 1941 with 600 people locked inside. There is a memorial to 400 Latvians who saved Jews during the Holocaust.

voyage.name: Russian Orthodox Church of the Annunciation
Jesus Church
voyage.content: An unusually-designed Lutheran church.

voyage.name: Latvian Academy of Sciences
voyage.content: Built in 1953, this building is often called "Stalin's Birthday Cake" because of its austere yet ornamented design. The 17th-floor balcony is open to visitors.

voyage.name: Riga Ghetto Museum
voyage.content: The museum, which encompasses a relocated historic wooden house and cobblestones from the Jewish ghetto created by Nazi Germany in occupied Riga during the Second World War, documents both the history of the ghetto and the tragic fates of Riga's Jewish population who perished in the Holocaust. It also attempts to recall Jewish community life from before the war.

voyage.name: Red warehouses
voyage.content: A huge cluster of mid-19th century warehouses between the train station and Central Market. They remind of the former trade harbor.

voyage.name: Esplanade Park
voyage.content: Designed by Georg Kuphaldt, who was expelled by Germany in 1915 as a spy because he had a telescope in his garden.

voyage.name: Koncertzāle Ave Sol
voyage.content: Hosts the renowned choral ensemble Ave Sol. The hall also plays host to a range of other concert activities.

voyage.name: Riga Central Market
voyage.hours: Different hours for different parts, see website for info
voyage.content: Noticeable for its huge hangars, built from parts of actual Zeppelin hangars bought for the market in 1920. The market has also a large open-air area. It deals mostly in fresh food and is a good place for fresh local fruit and vegetables, like mushrooms, berries and tomatoes – especially during summer and fall. The market is quite non-touristy but very good for souvenirs. There are lots of small cafes scattered

voyage.name: Galerija Istaba
voyage.content: Nice local artwork can be found here. There is also a small cafe/bar on the second floor with a nice, laid-back atmosphere.

voyage.name: Stockmann
voyage.content: The Latvian branch of the Finnish department store chain.

voyage.name: Bergs Bazaar
voyage.content: The Bergs bazaar is a 19th-century courtyard passage with a number of fashion boutiques, restaurants and a farmers' and crafts market on the second and fourth Saturday of each month.

voyage.name: Vermanitis
voyage.price: Fried fish €3, salmon steak €5, half chicken €2.50, large side of mashed potatoes or pasta €1, 500 ml beer €2.10
voyage.content: A fantastic range of Latvian food in "authentic" environment.

voyage.name: La Kanna
voyage.content: Modern and cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Milda
voyage.content: Eastern European cuisine. Only 20 seats.

voyage.name: Café Osiris
voyage.content: An artsy cafe with a cool interior, fireplace and pancakes worth killing for. While there, drop by Gallerija Istaba for another cup of coffee or beer, and make sure to check out some of the artwork sold downstairs.

voyage.name: Singh's
voyage.content: Great Indian food.

voyage.name: Stargorod
voyage.content: Traditional Czech and Latvian cousine, brewery, beer, tours in brewery, entertainment

voyage.name: Bergs
voyage.content: The restaurant of the hotel Bergs may be just about the best that Latvia has to offer. The food can be described as a fusion of Latvian and Western European cuisine. Menus are seasonal, and the ingredients always fresh - meaning sometimes not everything on the menu is available. With impeccable food and service, it is a wonder this place has not yet received the first Michelin star of any restaurant in Latvia.

voyage.name: Vincents
voyage.content: If you're splashing out try Vincents Restaurant which compares favorably to any up market western restaurant at half the price.

voyage.name: Galerija Istaba
voyage.content: Literally, room. An art gallery with a small café with 5 tables. Popular for its cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Miit Coffee
voyage.content: Great coffee and vegetarian food, with gluten-free options. Try the pancake brunch on Saturday and Sunday

voyage.name: French Bar
voyage.content: One of the cheapest, smallest, and oldest bars in Riga. It is popular among foreigners and local students. TV shows international sports matches.

voyage.name: Leningrad
voyage.content: Serves Latvian beers and food.

voyage.name: Skyline Bar
voyage.content: Just perfect view at sunset. Finding a table next to the windows might be difficult after 23:00. Cover charge at popular times.

voyage.name: Neo Bars
voyage.content: Enjoy the view of Riga from the 10th floor of the Central Station clock tower. Drinks, cocktails, European and Japanese cuisine. You need to take the elevator from the Central Station ground floor to the 8th to 10th floor.

voyage.name: Elizabeth's Youth Hostel
voyage.price: Dorm bed: €10 (low season), €12 (high season); single: €20 (low season), €28 (high season)
voyage.content: HI Hostel.

voyage.name: Mr. Hostel
voyage.content: Friendly and laid back. Free coffee and tea. Close to the old city.

voyage.name: Barons City Central Hostel
voyage.content: Australian & Latvian owned. 24-hour reception.

voyage.name: Riga Style Hostel
voyage.content: On a top floor of a 100-year-old historic building.

voyage.name: Tiger Hostel
voyage.content: The décor is extremely ugly - even for 1970s style. Free coffee and tea.

voyage.name: Posh Backpackers Hostel
voyage.content: Despite the name, the hostel is not posh at all. Privates, doubles, and 6-, 8-, and 12-bed dorms.

voyage.name: Hotel Edvards
voyage.content: Opened in September 2008, cosy, family-run hotel in a renovated 19th-century building.

voyage.name: Krisjanis and Gertrude Bed & Breakfast
voyage.content: Homely, popular with artists and musicians, city centre, en-suite rooms.

voyage.name: Mercure Riga Centre
voyage.content: Interesting postmodern decor based on the neighbourhood's Art Nouveau heritage. Additional charge for parking.

voyage.name: Tallink Hotel Riga
voyage.content: 256 rooms. Clean and modern.

voyage.name: Hotel Bergs
voyage.content: Great service, modern rooms, fitness center, and a small sauna.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Elizabete Hotel
voyage.content: Contemporary style.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Hotel Latvija
voyage.content: The largest business and conference hotel in the Baltics. With 27 floors, this hotel is noticeable on the Riga skyline.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Ridzene Hotel
voyage.content: A sombre, and slightly dated, Radisson next to the Esplanade

voyage.name: Hanza Hotel
voyage.content: 3-star hotel in Riga center.

voyage.name: Westa
voyage.content: The rooms are clean, private, safe, spacious, and have private bathrooms. Next to a market for food and clothing.

voyage.name: Grebenshchikov Church
voyage.content: An Old Believers' church.

voyage.name: Riga Motor Museum
voyage.content: Contains former vehicles of Stalin, Kruschev, and Brezhnev.

voyage.name: Riga Ethnographic Open Air Museum
voyage.content: The museum is in Jugla, near a lake of the same name. There are many traditional Latvian countryside houses collected in a forest/park and exhibitions inside them about the traditional things. The employees are often dressed in the traditional Latvian costumes, creating a nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: St. Paul's Church
voyage.content: Neogothic church from 1885 marks the center of Riga's main industrial neighbourhood. Most of the mural paintings are from 1930s and represent the art of independent Latvia before World War II.

voyage.name: Gas storage buildings
voyage.content: Two gas storage buildings from 1882 and 1901 (end of Matīsa iela) are landmarks of the old gas factory in Riga. These enormous structures reaching 40 m in diameter are probably the largest buildings of their kind in Eastern Europe. Note the pressure meter that mimics a clock.

voyage.name: Baptist church
voyage.content: Light neo-Romanic building from 1867 looks completely alien to its dark industrial neighborhood.

voyage.name: Twin water towers
voyage.content: These beautiful water towers were built by Oto Intce and Rūdolfs Frišs in 1896–1897 and were the first water towers built in Riga. Surprisingly, one of these is the only water tower still in use to this day. They are known among locals as Anna and Zhanna (Ann and Joan). Legend has it that Anna was a skilled quack in medieval Riga. She was accused of being a witch and burnt to death. This caused her sister Zhanna to c

voyage.name: Matisa cemetery
voyage.content: Matisa cemetery adjacent to the water towers has an interesting monument to the Latvian revolutionary heroes of the Russian Revolution of 1905. The monument was built in 1956-59 and consists of a long wall with haut-relief of Latvian revolutionaries and some poets' epitaphs. The cemetery also has a small monument to the victims of the 1940-1941 period of the Soviet occupation.

voyage.name: Russo-Balt factory
voyage.content: Valmieras iela and adjacent streets boast gorgeous industrial buildings from late 19th century. The largest factory was Russo-Balt that produced first cars and airplanes in the Russian empire. Most of these buildings are now abandoned and derelict but quite interesting to see. You will find lots of old plaques, signboards and other 100-year-old artifacts.

voyage.name: Čiekurkalns district
voyage.content: Čiekurkalns is a pleasant residential area on the outskirts of Riga. Despite the intense industrial development in the vicinity, most of the historical wooden architecture build in the end of XIX century has been preserved.

voyage.name: Mežaparks district
voyage.content: Forest Park is a pleasant park area on the outskirts of Riga. There are large, gorgeous residential houses once inhabited by Riga's prewar elite during the summers. They were largely let go during Soviet times but many are now being refurbished, repainted, and brought back to their original glory.

voyage.name: RVR train factory
voyage.content: One of the largest machine-building plants in Latvia, founded in 1895. RVR is based in Riga and was for many years the largest producer of electric and diesel trains and also tramcars in the former Soviet Union.

voyage.name: St. Francis Church
voyage.content: Built in 1892, a gorgeous neo-Gothic building in the middle of slums. Features copies of Giotto's mural paintings in the Papal Basilica of St. Francis of Assisi.

voyage.name: All Saints Church
voyage.content: Orthodox church built in neo-Romanic style around 1880. Unlike other orthodox churches in Latvia, which are typically Russian in their style and nature, this one was designed by a Latvian architect.

voyage.name: Church of John the Baptist
voyage.content: Construction started in 1913-14 but it was not finished before the Russian Revolution and continued in 1920s when Latvia became independent. This led to a strange mix of styles rendering the church a rare example of modernist architecture implemented in an Orthodox temple. The adjacent Ivanovskoe cemetery is the main Orthodox cemetery of Riga.

voyage.name: Church of Our Lady of Kazan
voyage.content: Another church on the same cemetery. Build of wood in 1812-15 in a somewhat awkward style with 5 small domes sitting on a massive drum.

voyage.name: Church of Gregory the Illuminator
voyage.content: Armenian church built in 2011.

voyage.name: Old New Synagogue
voyage.content: The only synagogue that survived through World War II. Built in 1889, partially restored after the war and converted into a residential building.

voyage.name: Church of Michael Archangel
voyage.content: Old Believers church from 1894-95, nice example of the Russian Revival style.

voyage.name: Horse-drawn omnibus
voyage.content: A funny monument commemorating the first Riga tram that was driven by horse power. An old iron construction nearby reminds of the former Hay Market.

voyage.name: Old Jewish cemetery
voyage.content: A huge area that reminds of the Jewish population of Latgales apkaime. Established in early 18th century, this cemetery kept expanding till the beginning of 20th century. After all local Jews were exterminated by the Nazis during World War II, Soviet government destroyed the remaining gravestones and converted the area into a Park of Communist Brigades. Now there is a small Jewish memorial.

voyage.name: Riga Zoo
voyage.content: The Riga Zoo is small, but fairly popular.

voyage.name: Arena Riga
voyage.content: An indoor sports arena and concert venue. Notable as the home rink of the city's ice hockey team Dinamo Riga, playing in the KHL, the arena is also where the world's greatest pop and rock artists and bands hold their Riga concerts.

voyage.name: Lido Entertainment Center
voyage.price: Cafeteria: €3.30 for a meat main course and €0.70 for a plateload of roast potatoes. Pancakes for €0.60. Top floor: Buffet for set price of €16
voyage.hours: Main restaurant: daily 11:00-23:00, express restaurant: daily 13:00-23:00, beer cellar: Mon-Fri 18:00-00:00, holidays 12:00-00:00, playroom: Mon-Fri 17:00-22:00, holidays 12:00-22:00
voyage.content: The wooden building features three floors of dining, a built-in wooden windmill, and a small amusement park outside. The ground floor and basement operate cafeteria-style. There is a huge choice available, including a variety of soups including borscht and the Latvian cold beetroot soup, as well as kebabs, breasts, chicken sausages, fish, red meats. Blinis are another specialty here.

voyage.name: Fontaine Delisnack
voyage.content: Fast food, open 24/7.

voyage.name: Ezītis miglā (Avotu iela)
voyage.content: Reasonably priced drinks and food, nice atmosphere.

voyage.name: Šašliki Mangaļos
voyage.content: Popular with locals. They offer shashlik on a skewer with a choice of chicken, lamb or beef, with tomato sauce and a side of vegetables or Armenian flatbread. Beverage options include various local beers, Georgian wine or softdrinks. Indoor and outdoor seating. The indoor furniture looks like it has already seen the days of the barricades. Self-service, basic Latvian is recommended. € 14 for a skewer of pork, sauce,

voyage.name: Godvil
voyage.content: Nightclub.

voyage.name: Alus Bārs
voyage.content: A very local bar, literally "the beer bar". Like going back in time to the turbulent 1990s. Open Monday to Saturday from 12:00 to anytime in the evening from 19:00 to 23:00.A can of Cēsu €2.2050 cl of Mītava €2.5050 cl of Piebalgas €3Sometimes also offer fries and small sandwiches.

voyage.name: Apartment Hotel Riga
voyage.content: Apartments on Riga's main street. Every apartment has either two separate beds or one double, as well as a washing machine, television, gas ring, air conditioner, refrigerator, and set of dishes.

voyage.name: Days Hotel Riga VEF
voyage.content: Part of the Wyndham/Days Inn chain. A great option if you don't need to be within walking distance of the center.

voyage.name: Dodo Hotel
voyage.content: Modern rooms with shower, WC, flat-screen TV, and hairdryer. French owned.

voyage.name: Ķīpsala
voyage.content: An island in the city centre with Nordic dwelling architecture and a beach that is very popular in the summer.

voyage.name: Riga TV Tower
voyage.content: A 368-m-high tower built of concrete and standing on three legs, this is the tallest tower in the European Union. However, it is closed to the public as of October 2026.

voyage.name: National Library
voyage.content: An important part of the West Bank's cityscape, the National Library was built in 2008-13. It is perhaps the most remarkable part of the "New Riga" giving a more gentle feel to skyscrapers and other high-tech buildings that have been constructed on the West Bank of the Daugava since independence. The building was nicknamed the "Castle of Light" (Gaismas Pils), and the architect intended to mimic the towers of Vecriga

voyage.name: Riga Aviation Museum
voyage.content: Bored at the airport? Check out the Riga Aviation museum, which contains several rare aircraft.

voyage.name: University of Latvia Botanical Garden
voyage.hours: Apr-Sep 09:00-19:00, other months 10:00-16:30, Butterfly House has shorter opening hours (check website)
voyage.content: The Botanical Garden is quite large and featuring an impressively broad and well-cultivated collection of plant species. The long history of the garden is reflected in its rich built heritage. There is a butterfly house within the garden's grounds, where you can experience free-flying tropical butterflies. Apart from botanical interests, the garden is simply beautiful and great for a stroll.

voyage.name: Wooden architecture of Āgenskalns
voyage.content: Very nice part of Pārdaugava with old wooden buildings, which date back to the 18th-19th centuries and are still preserved in between Nometņu, Slokas, Eduarda Smiļģa and Talsu streets. This unusual place is the pearl of Pārdaugava’s wooden architecture, a visit to it will bring an unforgettable aesthetic pleasure. You may start with getting off at the stop “Smiļģa iela” tram #2. There are also nice wooden buildings o

voyage.name: Latvian Railway History Museum
voyage.content: Exhibits several collections of Soviet rolling stock.

voyage.name: Theatre Museum
voyage.content: Located in the eccentrically designed and furnished pre-war house of a former director of Riga Daile Theatre and one of the key figures in Latvian theatre of the 20th century.

voyage.name: St. Martin's Church
voyage.content: Lutheran church from 1850s. Its decorations are fairly plain, but the location among the trees is remarkable.

voyage.name: Baptist Church
voyage.content: A mix of cultures and styles. Built in 1913-16, this church had neither a tower nor a dome and resembled a simple residential building. The tower was added in 1936. Baptist services continued until 1961 and resumed shortly after Latvia re-gained its independence.

voyage.name: Trinity church
voyage.content: A fine example of Russian style from the very end of 19th century. Don't miss rich decorations as well as eye-catching mural paintings and icons inside.

voyage.name: Methodist church
voyage.content: A fairly bland building from 1930s. However, the very presence of a big Methodist church in Riga is remarkable.

voyage.name: Church of St. Albert
voyage.content: Baroque edifice from early 20th century. The interior of the church was partly designed in 1950s despite the official atheist propaganda that was widely imposed in the Soviet Union.

voyage.name: Āgenskalns Market
voyage.content: This is a smaller counterpart to the Central Market, to be found the central square of Āgenskalns on the left bank of Daugava, which is a crossing of no less than 6 streets. An impressive building from 1911-23, remarkable as a red-brick manifestation of Jugendstil architecture in Riga. While the offerings are decisively not geared towards tourists, you may want to visit just to experience the historic low-rise neighb

voyage.name: Ķīpsala Island Student Cafeteria
voyage.content: Several sets of home-like food are offered in a cozy atmosphere.

voyage.name: Čili Pica
voyage.content: The Latvian pizza chain has three restaurants in Pardaugava.

voyage.name: Lido Spice
voyage.content: The Rigan buffet restaurant chain also has a restaurant in the Spice shopping mall.

voyage.name: Ciemakukulis
voyage.content: A cozy café with a truly delicious selection of baked goods. Free wifi.

voyage.name: Riga City Camping
voyage.price: Per person €3; per tent site: €6; per camper site €7-10; car parking: €3.
voyage.content: Open May 15 to September 15. Nice facilities.

voyage.name: Two Wheels
voyage.content: Classy hotel/hostel across the river from the old town.

voyage.name: Primo Hotel
voyage.price: Single €35/€45 (low season/high season); double/twin €40/€50 (low season/high season), family room €70 (up to 4 persons); breakfast €5 extra
voyage.content: Modern 3-star hotel, free parking, cable TV, only en suite rooms.

voyage.name: Sky-High Hotel
voyage.price: Twin room €59.50 without breakfast, €70 breakfast included
voyage.content: A basic clean and functional motel mostly used by air crew, the main advantage is that it's an easy walking distance from the airport terminal. It may be a good one-night stay if you are arriving very late or leaving very early.

voyage.name: Radisson Blu Daugava Hotel
voyage.content: On the left bank of the Daugava, with views of the Old Town.
